text:
maria: Heads up — need final sign-off on the customer key lifecycle protocol for Private deployments. Main open items: RBAC change window for KMS ops, audit log retention SLA and immutability, rotation escrow (who can access), and vuln/incident triage when key material may be exposed. Can Platform/Legal/Product weigh in?

kevin: We should minimize RBAC blast radius. Proposal: scoped service accounts + short-lived role assumption. Ops get `kms:maintenance` only during authorized windows and require 2-person approval for any rotation. Example policy snippet below for discussion.

```
# example (conceptual) role binding
role: kms_maintenance
principals:
  - serviceAccount:platform-kms-maintainer
  - group:sec-oncall
conditions:
  - type: time_window
    value: "wed:02:00-06:00 UTC"
  - type: approval_count
    value: 2
```

sam: From product/customer perspective we need two distinct modes: `customer-managed-only` (we never have access; customer rotates) and `co-managed` (we can coordinate rotates with explicit consent / signed authorization). SLA and UX differ for each.

priya: Legal notes — SOC2/ISO require immutable audit trails; retention baseline should be 1 year but recommend offering 3 years for enterprise customers. Contract must specify who maintains the logs and WORM assurances. Two-person control for rotation looks good; add requirement for HSM attestation (FIPS cert) if customer asks.

raj: Customers keep asking: if they suspect compromise, how fast can we rotate? They want an emergency path they can trigger. Should be customer-initiated immediate revoke + emergency rotate with signed auth and POA (proof-of-authority). Also need clear communication templates.

maria: Agreed. Draft incident triage steps for key compromise: 1) immediate revoke/disable key; 2) snapshot audit logs to WORM storage; 3) start isolated forensic cluster; 4) notify customer + regulatory contacts per CL clause. Add runbook `kms-emergency-rotate` with exact commands and checklist.

kevin: Operational details: stream KMS audit logs to S3 with server-side encryption + S3 Object Lock enabled for WORM. Logs must include `requester_identity`, `requester_ip`, `operation`, `key_fingerprint`, and an integrity `pre/post_state_hash`. Example log line format for clarity: 

```
{"ts":"2026-05-01T02:15:03Z","requester":"serviceAccount:platform-kms-maintainer","ip":"18.206.12.4","op":"RotateKey","key_id":"cust-abc123","pre_hash":"a1b2...","post_hash":"c3d4...","approval_ids":["ticket-324","sig-938"]}
```

maria: For RBAC change window — propose a 4-hour weekly maintenance window (low traffic) for planned rotations/patches, with pre-notification and telemetry dashboard to monitor errors. All RBAC escalations outside that window require emergency ticket + sec-oncall approval.

priya: Also flag data residency: for EU customers ensure key material never leaves customer VPC or region unless explicitly authorized. Contract must list wrap algorithms and export rules. We'll draft clause for rotation authority and escrow conditions.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: new runbook created: https://go/internal/runbooks/kms_emergency_rotate (ops-only link) :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: infra-bot: S3 bucket `rw-kms-logs-prod` now has Object Lock enabled in compliance mode (retention 3y) — pending verification.

kevin: 👍 I'll draft the RBAC policy, PIR for log pipeline, and a PR for runbook updates. Aim to post by EOD.

maria: Thanks. @priya please draft the contractual clause; @raj collect customer asks and edge cases. We'll reconvene tomorrow 10:00 UTC to sign off.
thread_summary: Short thread discussing customer key lifecycle protocol: RBAC maintenance windows, two-person approval for rotations, audit log WORM retention, customer vs co-managed modes, incident triage runbook, and action items for drafting policies and contract clauses.
